reason: E1 directly supports the formation of a denser Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 oxide layer and improved corrosion resistance at ~10 at.% Al, but the cited study was performed under PWR operating conditions, not high-temperature steam oxidation (LOCA). E2 only provides general background on ATF cladding challenges and does not supply specific evidence for the key premises. The hypothesis therefore overstates the direct applicability of E1's findings to LOCA conditions.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings can be deposited on Zr-alloy substrates by RF magnetron co-sputtering
Increasing Al content to ~10 at.% in AlNbTiZr MEA coating yields the best corrosion resistance and minimum oxygen penetration depth
The improved corrosion resistance at ~10 at.% Al originates from a denser oxide layer of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
The cited corrosion resistance results are relevant to high-temperature steam oxidation under LOCA conditions
